defect: A startup owner could submit an unguarded migration after another owner upgraded the schema. Successful stale index or table-rebuild DDL reset the committed marker backwards.
correction: A temporary aggregate CHECK enforces exactly one expected predecessor before DDL in the same captured transaction. Stale work rolls back and adopts the authoritative newer marker. A known future marker remains explicitly unsupported.
formats: No persistent schema, schema-version or RPC-format change.

negative.review_overlay: Two regressions appended to the original console storage fixture plus a filtered build-only Persistent target. Exact patch is retained.
negative.test_root_optimization: Debug, as in the normal native test graph; dependencies use ReleaseSafe.
negative.storage_path: Actual Persistent.open and Node.exec captured transactions, not an unmanaged SQLite connection.

guarded.review_overlay: Build-only filtered root at console_migrations_test.zig with explicit ReleaseSafe optimization. Production files match the committed fix.
properties: Stale migrations5 and37 preserve current marker and retained minute bytes.
Every historical catalog migration rejects stale replay at the supported version.
Valid predecessor advances once; stale retry adopts the committed marker.
Mid-body SQL failure rolls back all schema and data effects.
Empty, multiple and NULL marker rows fail before body effects.
A future marker appearing after the advisory read remains explicitly unsupported.
No main or TEMP guard object remains, checked against the still-open actual writer.
Reopening the captured store preserves data and marker; recovered-writer cleanup is checked again.

normal_daemon.build_graph: Original unmodified build.zig. No filters, skips, timer changes or test assertions removed.
normal_daemon.test_revision_note: The normal gate preceded the additional live-writer TEMP premise; the final focused ReleaseSafe gate verifies that stronger assertion. Runtime guard and Persistent catalog import are identical.

limits: The source-level race is reproduced independently. These results do not identify the earlier .19 startup refusal cause, qualify clustered RPC replay, or replace final combined cluster/platform gates. No performance claim is made.
